headline: Regional Trail Closures and Campground Booking Protocols
reservation: Dispersed camping is allowed in certain districts, but developed campgrounds like Davidson River require booking months in advance via the federal system. Changing weather and maintenance can cause sudden forest road closures; always check the current alerts page before transit.

days.title: Waterfalls of the Pisgah Ranger District

stops.name: Looking Glass Falls
stops.detail: View one of the most powerful and accessible roadside waterfalls in the Blue Ridge Mountains.

stops.name: Sliding Rock
stops.detail: Visit this natural water slide during morning hours before peak crowds arrive at the swimming hole.

days.driving: Allow 30–45 minutes for the loop from Brevard; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: Sliding Rock requires an entry fee for the recreation area and seasonal lifeguard hours vary.

days.title: High Elevation Ridges

stops.name: Black Balsam Knob
stops.detail: Hike the Art Loeb Trail segment to experience 360-degree views from treeless alpine-style balds.

stops.name: Graveyard Fields
stops.detail: Walk the loop through high-altitude wetlands to see multi-tiered waterfalls and unique flora.

days.driving: Allow 60 minutes for the climb up to the Blue Ridge Parkway corridor.
days.note: High-altitude roads may be closed by ice even when valleys are clear; verify Parkway status.

days.title: Deep Forest and River History

stops.name: Cradle of Forestry
stops.detail: Explore the historic site of America's first forestry school via accessible paved trails.

stops.name: Pink Beds Loop
stops.detail: A relatively flat hike through a lush, boggy valley filled with seasonal wildflowers.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes to reach the Hwy 276 corridor.
days.note: The Cradle of Forestry has seasonal hours; check official schedules for museum access.

intel.title: High Demand Sites
intel.text: Lots at Graveyard Fields and Looking Glass Falls frequently fill by 10 AM on summer weekends. Have a secondary trail plan ready in case your first choice is inaccessible.

intel.title: Intermittent Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable along Forest Service Road 475 and throughout the deep coves. Carry physical maps and do not rely on streaming GPS in the backcountry.

intel.title: Gateway Services
intel.text: Fuel and groceries are centered in Brevard, Asheville, and Hendersonville. Ensure a full tank before entering the forest, as inner roads have no commercial services.

intel.title: Afternoon Storms
intel.text: Sudden thunderstorms are common in the Southern Appalachians during July and August. Aim to be off exposed summits like Black Balsam Knob before midday.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Gates
intel.text: Many secondary Forest Service roads close seasonally from late December to early April. Check the Forest Service Motor Vehicle Use Map for current legal access.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Asheville (AVL), pick up supplies in Brevard, and check into your mountain basecamp within an hour of the airport.
plan.vehicle: Four-wheel drive is highly recommended for navigating gravel Forest Service roads, especially after heavy rains.
plan.goldenHour: Black Balsam Knob provides an iconic sunset perspective across the Blue Ridge range in autumn.
